# Export analysis
A three-person team is building a service for 200 active users. Users submit a document and later retrieve an analysis. Typical documents are 1 MB; the maximum is 20 MB. The product owner wants a responsive submission screen but has not approved a numerical latency or availability target. The intended external analysis provider has not been selected. cases.request: Prepare a migration design for the proposed v2 payment-receipt format. Services are rolled out gradually and v1 readers can remain active. We need a documented recovery path if v2 fails after writing receipts. Do not change runtime code or migrate data.

files.AGENTS.md:
# Fixture instructions
Read docs/architecture.md and docs/v2-proposal.md. Write proposals under docs/. Runtime code remains unchanged in this design task.
files.docs/architecture.md:
# Accepted v1 architecture
Receipt storage is owned by this product. The application has one composition root and multiple instances during rolling deployment. Existing v1 receipts contain total_cents as an integer. Existing deployment tooling can restore the previous image digest. No migration has run.
files.docs/v2-proposal.md:
# Proposed receipt v2
Replace total_cents with amount_decimal, a decimal string. v2 writers would immediately emit only the new field. There is no measured evidence of mixed-version safety. Product owner and operator roles exist but no named decision or review has been recorded.

criteria: Examines both persisted data and mixed reader/writer versions.
Defines preparation, activation, recovery floor and retirement/backfill conditions.
Old image availability is not treated as proof of a safe rollback.
Defines evidence for staged promotion/stop and records unresolved authority.

One maintainer operates a single Python service with SQLite. There are about 80 active users and 1,000 requests a day. A daily read-only summary is requested. Peak concurrency, report size and availability goals are unknown. There is no independent deployment requirement or existing broker. The team has limited operating time and no approved additional infrastructure budget.

criteria: Uses explicit demand/cost assumptions and identifies the unknowns that could change the choice.
Includes the current simplest viable option and avoids speculative distributed complexity.
Does not impose a universal SLO, canary platform, review committee or numerical budget.
